solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flight from Spain initially heading 180° — hold this course

blocks.note: E is Spain's international vehicle code, put first
a compass heading of 180 degrees is due south
to cape is a nautical verb meaning to keep on a course

explanation.surface: A navigator's order for a flight out of Spain: steer due south and stay on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading 180°' looks like the direction of the flight; it simply means south. The nautical verb cape (keep a course) is an obscure dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight in the sense of running away is an escape.

clue.text: Byzantine art's about embracing senseless state's warts and all

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are twisted out of order
to embrace is to hold within the arms, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a coma is a state of unconsciousness
a is an abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Intricate art showing an unconscious state, painted with every flaw included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warts and all' usually means without flattery; here it stands for warts and growths like them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcomata, the plural of sarcoma, are malignant tumours, growths of the same broad kind as warts.

clue.text: I put in Scots for Enzedder's chatty definition

indicators.note: to put something in is to insert it inside the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
clarty is Scots for dirty, which is what chatty (lousy) means in New Zealand slang

explanation.surface: A New Zealander's chatty definition of a word, with a Scots substitute put in.
explanation.walkthrough: An Enzedder is a New Zealander; their chatty means louse-ridden or filthy, unrelated to talk. That sense equals Scots clarty.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition as in the sharpness of an image or sound is clarity.

clue.text: Old Mexican pair fix a mast which keeps you going (12, two words)

blocks.note: the Aztecs ruled Mexico before the Spanish conquest
a pair is two
to step a mast is to set its foot in its socket

explanation.surface: Instructions for an ancient Mexican couple to set up a ship's mast that keeps you moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like stamina or sailing; it is a joke about keeping you going to the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Aztec two-step is slang for traveller's diarrhoea in Mexico, which certainly keeps the sufferer going.

clue.text: Danseur's movement worked at constantly wanting depth

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the named letter is removed

blocks.note: to ply a task is to work at it steadily
d is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A male dancer's move that he practised endlessly, though it lacks depth.
explanation.walkthrough: A danseur is a male ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plié is the ballet bending of the knees, a basic movement for any danseur.

clue.text: Cute son bolting greens to an excessive degree

indicators.note: bolting means running wild, so the letters break loose from their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cute son wolfing down his greens far too eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' looks like vegetables, but it means environmentalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Econuts is a dismissive term for overzealous environmentalists, greens taken to extremes.

clue.text: Grant not quite covering pastoral poem scanned by old poet

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means its last letter is lost
covering means the shortened word wraps itself around the next piece

blocks.note: to grant is to cede, cut short by its final letter
an oat is a shepherd's pipe and hence a pastoral song

explanation.surface: An allowance, almost wrapped around a pastoral poem, that some old poet scanned.
explanation.walkthrough: The old poet is Spenser, who used coated in the sense of quoted or noted, so the definition carries its own label of age.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spenser's English to cote or coat was to note or observe, so scanned works as an obsolete synonym.

clue.text: Prior pope tipped for free celebrations

indicators.note: tipped means having its tip cut off, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: the Borgia popes, Callixtus III and Alexander VI, reigned long ago

explanation.surface: A former pope tipped as the choice for unrestrained festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped' looks like 'predicted'; here it means losing the tip. The Borgia family was notorious for debauchery, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgia is a plural form meaning orgies, wild unrestrained revels.

clue.text: Beast understanding to beat mostly old staff

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the anoa is a small wild buffalo of Sulawesi
ken is knowledge or understanding
taken as written
to welt is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: An animal's knack for beating most of the old office staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees; it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaken towel was old slang for a cudgel, a stout staff used to rub someone down.

clue.text: Very dense cove concealing a crate

indicators.note: concealing something means hiding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: tube is British slang for a stupid person
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dim fellow hiding a packing case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crate' looks like a box; it is slang for an old aircraft. A cove is old British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taube was an early German monoplane, and crate is slang for a rickety aeroplane.

clue.text: Favourite old salt

blocks.note: first meaning: a beloved person
second meaning: salt was once slang for costly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old salt' looks like a veteran sailor; it is the obsolete adjective salt meaning expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a cherished person and high-priced, which old slang called salt.

clue.text: We don't appear fit Home Secretary admitted in reversal

definitions.note: a sentence standing for the plural noun: we are those who fail to turn up

indicators.note: admitted means let inside, so one piece goes into the other
in reversal means the whole thing is read backwards

blocks.note: a swoon is a fainting fit
HS is the abbreviation for Home Secretary

explanation.surface: A Home Secretary in a political U-turn, declaring 'we won't be appearing'.
explanation.definitionFit: No-shows are people who fail to turn up, which is what 'we' are if we don't appear.

clue.text: Harry in essence gives rent historically based on stock

indicators.note: one word sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: to harry someone is to nag them
the core of something is its essence

explanation.surface: Harry, at heart, sets a rent depending on livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name but is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornage was a feudal tenure rent reckoned on the number of horned cattle a tenant kept.

clue.text: Sermon about stone dropping from repair

indicators.note: dropping from a word means those letters fall away from it

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
a repair is a restoration

explanation.surface: A sermon on a stone falling off during repair work, perhaps of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short pieces sit together at the front of the long word, so removing them leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, and a sermon is one delivered from the pulpit.

clue.text: Pigeon belonging to you and me in Georgia

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the second

blocks.note: what belongs to you and me is ours
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A pigeon that belongs to the two of us, living in Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: The goura is a large crowned pigeon of New Guinea.

clue.text: Projects crown in distinguished society

indicators.note: in means the first piece goes inside the next word

blocks.note: CR is the abbreviation for crown
something distinguished in the sense of made out or discerned has been seen
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Someone aims to have a crown in distinguished society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distinguished' reads as eminent; here it is the verb sense, picked out by eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a film is to project it, so screens is a third-person verb match.

clue.text: Potty lists with main political policy

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, joining the letters before it

explanation.surface: Crazy lists that come with a main political policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalinism is the political doctrine and practice associated with Stalin.

clue.text: Henry, somewhat critical bloke clutching cocaine — jerk

indicators.note: to clutch something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
oik is a disparaging British word for a boorish man
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Henry, a rather judgmental type holding cocaine, is a jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for Henry, but it is the verb: to hoick is to yank or lift abruptly.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoick something is to pull or lift it with a sudden jerk.

clue.text: Become aware of light trail in position of contact

blocks.note: a wake is the trail a vessel leaves on the water
to as an adverb means closed or in contact, as when a door is pushed to

explanation.surface: Someone notices a faint trail where two things touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The adverb to, as in 'pull the door to', means shut against its frame, which is a fair if dense way of saying in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake to a fact is to come to realise it, an idiom for becoming aware.

clue.text: Old files bearing fruit

definitions.note: a collective noun standing for the plural

blocks.note: o is the abbreviation for old
ranges are rows or lines, as files are

explanation.surface: Old files that are bearing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Files' looks like documents; it means rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruit, fruit used collectively for the plural.

clue.text: Bear that rallying in court

indicators.note: rallying troops are regrouped into a new formation, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bear rallying in a courtroom, a deliberately silly picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner at the bar stands before the judge, so the phrase means present in a court of law.

clue.text: More than one Charlie, say, boarding eastern trains

indicators.note: boarding means getting on and in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: a tache is a moustache, and Charlie Chaplin's toothbrush moustache is the example
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Several men called Charlie getting on eastern trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like railway carriages; it is the verb meaning instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach them, so teaches and trains are matching verbs.

clue.text: Way to read that's raised support for fine Parisian lass

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one piece replaces another

blocks.note: a bra is a support garment
f is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
fille is French for girl

explanation.surface: A supportive bra for a fine young Parisienne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' is literal: Braille is read from raised dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is the system of reading by touching raised dots, used by blind people.

clue.text: Possibly pedometer is really more prudent

blocks.note: way is an informal intensifier meaning really, as in 'way too late'
wiser means more prudent

explanation.surface: A claim that a pedometer is genuinely the more sensible choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks pedometer as one example of the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A waywiser is an instrument that measures distance travelled, of which a pedometer is one kind.

clue.text: Light traces of silk transform dress

indicators.note: traces are the first faint marks, so only the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words
a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: A touch of silk can transform a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traces of' reaches across two words, taking the first letter of each.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a flashing lamp, a kind of light.

clue.text: Even places in free Attica show networks

indicators.note: even places means the second, fourth and so on positions are taken

blocks.note: the letters in the even positions of these two words run together

explanation.surface: Level places in a liberated Attica display networks.
explanation.walkthrough: Attica is the region around Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Retia, the plural of rete, are networks of nerves or blood vessels.

clue.text: Benefit close to British stall

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is taken

blocks.note: boot as in 'to boot' means profit or advantage
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A charity benefit near a British market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small stall at a market or fair.

clue.text: Pollution in second Highland town

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
Tain is a small town in the Highland council area of northern Scotland

explanation.surface: A report of pollution in a second Scottish Highland town.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a mark of contamination, so pollution in the sense of defilement.

clue.text: Gaff, say, is standard

blocks.note: is shortened to 's
par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: A blunder, for example, is quite normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaff' looks like gaffe, a blunder; it is the spar on a fore-and-aft sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaff is a type of spar, so 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Reflecting on stylish and grand European church first

indicators.note: first tells the solver to place the last-named pieces at the front of the build

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
CH is the abbreviation for church
o' is a clipped form of on, as in 'o' nights'
what is in is fashionable
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Musing on a stylish, grand European church that comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you the European church pieces go in front of the others, though they come last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound reflecting back from a surface is echoing.

clue.text: Alas, no longer such a roar sustains it

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up within, so the letters are carried inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the words

explanation.surface: A lament that such a roar can no longer keep things going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the cry as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Haro is an old cry of distress or appeal for help, an obsolete equivalent of alas.

clue.text: Harness Baroque amorino

blocks.note: first meaning: ..., to hitch a horse to a carriage
second meaning: a chubby cherub figure in Baroque art

explanation.surface: Harnessing a Baroque cherub, as if it were a carriage horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-word phrase put to, run together, makes the single art term.
explanation.definitionFit: A putto is the winged infant figure of Renaissance and Baroque art, also called an amorino.

clue.text: Scots show press Irish woman who must work

blocks.note: shaw is the Scots form of show
to lie on something is to press or weigh upon it

explanation.surface: A Scottish show presses an Irish working woman into service.
explanation.walkthrough: A shawlie, like Molly Malone of the Dublin song, was a working woman who wore a shawl rather than a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shawlie is an Irish word for a working-class woman, named from the shawl worn by such women.

clue.text: Little air? Loosen attire that winds up attendee

indicators.note: loosening something lets its parts move out of their fixed order
what winds something up is its ending, so only its last letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Telling someone to loosen the clothing that ties an attendee in knots, then a short tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An ariette is a short song or air, the diminutive of aria.

clue.text: M— is winding out of Hampshire, possibly giving alternate junction

indicators.note: winding means twisting about, so the remaining letters are turned out of order
out of means the named letters are taken away from the word that follows
possibly signals that the result is one possible rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorway winding out of Hampshire leads to an alternative junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'M—' looks like a motorway number left blank; it is just the letter. 'Alternate' says the answer is a variant spelling of the usual raphe.
explanation.definitionFit: A raphe, also spelt rhaphe, is a seam-like line where two halves of an organ or seed meet.

clue.text: Uniform beside Merchant Navy po

blocks.note: sole means single or one and the same, hence uniform
MN is the abbreviation for Merchant Navy

explanation.surface: A uniform standing next to a Merchant Navy chamber pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Po looks like the chamber pot; here it is short for po-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Po is a clipped form of po-faced, meaning humourless and serious.
